name: select
title: Select
purpose: A native select as the control of a field, for one choice from a short fixed list.
whenToUse: For one choice from a list the app already knows: a base branch, a repository, a model.
When the list is too long to show as radio buttons, from about five options up.
whenNotToUse: For two to four options the reader should compare. Use a radio group.
For on or off. Use a checkbox.
For a list long enough to need searching, or for free text. Use a text input in a field.
For a menu of actions. Use buttons.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and as wide as the field. Limit the width on the field's container.

accessibility: Use a select element carrying both gw-field__control and gw-select__control, wrapped in an element with gw-select, inside gw-field. The wrapper only draws the chevron.
Give it a label element whose for attribute matches the select's id.
When nothing is chosen yet, make the first option an instruction with an empty value, such as Choose a repository, and set required on the select.
For an invalid choice, set aria-invalid="true" on the select and link a gw-field__error that says what to choose.
While the options load, set disabled, show one option that says what is loading, and say what is being fetched in the description. Remove disabled when the options arrive.
The keyboard is the browser's own: Space or Enter opens the list, the arrow keys move, typing jumps to a matching option, Escape closes.
The chevron is decoration drawn by the stylesheet. It needs no markup and takes no pointer events.
